prompt: Create a 16:10 desktop landing-page first-viewport design comp for Sentinel, a browser QA automation platform. Visual world: RELEASE PROOF — press-room preflight proofs and registration sheets, entirely original, no red, no orange, no gradients, no glass, no generic SaaS card wall. One saturated ultramarine proof sheet (#1527A4) owns most of the viewport; fluorescent chartreuse (#DAFF3F), near-black (#11131C), and cool paper gray (#ECEDE6) are the only supporting colors. Typography is bold condensed Swiss/industrial display plus clean humanist body, roman only. The page itself should feel like a release proof waiting for human sign-off. Integrate the real product mechanism into the composition: a horizontal run trace progresses through TEACH → REPLAY → EVIDENCE → HUMAN DECISION, with explicit checkpoint/stop markers. Main headline: “Teach the test once. Trust every release.” Supporting line: “Human-taught browser journeys. Safe replay. Complete evidence.” A clear “Join the pilot” control is positioned like an approval tab, and a secondary “Watch the walkthrough” action is visible. Include one large, plausible but clearly stylized product evidence panel showing a real Sentinel run timeline and screenshot, without fake browser traffic-light chrome. Navigation is edge-aligned/minimal, not centered-link SaaS navigation. No tiny illegible filler, no invented metrics, no customer logos, no testimonials. Strong asymmetric composition, visible registration ticks and proof annotations used sparingly, full-viewport commitment, polished award-level web art direction. This is a visual direction comp, not production code. Save or provide the generated asset as a WebP suitable for .impeccable/mocks/decision/assigned.webp.
